Topics · Is the Quran from God?

Why should I trust a book written 1,400 years ago?

Age proves nothing either way. So ask how a book could be tested. This one sets its own test. What follows?

Part 1 of 3

﴿أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ ۚ وَلَوْ كَانَ مِنْ عِندِ غَيْرِ ٱللَّهِ لَوَجَدُوا۟ فِيهِ ٱخْتِلَـٰفًا كَثِيرًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

Then do they not reflect upon the Qur’ān?[203] If it had been from [any] other than Allāh, they would have found within it much contradiction.

Translator's notes

[203] i.e., its meanings and its objective.

Quran · An-Nisa 4:82

Translation

“Every word of God is flawless. He is a shield to those who take refuge in him. Don’t you add to his words, lest he reprove you, and you be found a liar.

Original · Hebrew

כָּל־אִמְרַ֣ת אֱל֣וֹהַּ צְרוּפָ֑ה מָגֵ֥ן ה֝֗וּא לַֽחֹסִ֥ים בּֽוֹ׃ אַל־תּ֥וֹסְףְּ עַל־דְּבָרָ֑יו פֶּן־יוֹכִ֖יחַ בְּךָ֣ וְנִכְזָֽבְתָּ׃

Proverbs · 30:5-6

World English Bible

Age alone settles nothing. Some very old books are still right about geometry, and some are wrong about medicine. So the useful question is not how old a book is but what it claims and how that could fail. The Quran does something unusual here. It offers a condition against itself: if it came from anyone other than God, people would find much inconsistency in it. So it invites the search. There are hard cases, and you are entitled to see them.

A question for you

What would shake your trust in an old book most?

If you sayIf it got facts about the world wrong.
ThenThen your standard is fair. A whole question covers that, and the exaggerated claims too.
If you sayIf it commanded what my conscience sees as wrong.
ThenThat is a serious standard. The hard passages are not hidden here.
If you sayIf its text had changed over time.
ThenThen you want the history, all of it, and it has its own page.
If you sayIf the man who brought it could not be trusted.
ThenThat comes next.

Part 2 of 3

﴿قُل لَّوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مَا تَلَوْتُهُۥ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَآ أَدْرَىٰكُم بِهِۦ ۖ فَقَدْ لَبِثْتُ فِيكُمْ عُمُرًا مِّن قَبْلِهِۦٓ ۚ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "If Allāh had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you, for I had remained among you a lifetime before it.[516] Then will you not reason?"

Translator's notes

[516] The Prophet (ﷺ) lived among his people forty years before receiving any revelation.

Quran · Yunus 10:16

﴿بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّىٰٓ١ أَن جَآءَهُ ٱلْأَعْمَىٰ٢﴾

Translation of the meaning

He [i.e., the Prophet (ﷺ) ] frowned and turned away Because there came to him the blind man,[1853] [interrupting].

Translator's notes

[1853] ʿAbdullāh, the son of Umm Maktūm.

Quran · Abasa 80:1-2

Translation

“‘You shall not curse the deaf, nor put a stumbling block before the blind; but you shall fear your God. I am Yahweh.

Original · Hebrew

לֹא־תְקַלֵּ֣ל חֵרֵ֔שׁ וְלִפְנֵ֣י עִוֵּ֔ר לֹ֥א תִתֵּ֖ן מִכְשֹׁ֑ל וְיָרֵ֥אתָ מֵּאֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

the Torah (Leviticus) · 19:14

World English Bible

With any old document you can ask what kind of source it is. Two features stand out. The man who brought it lived among his people for decades before he brought any message, so they had his whole record to judge by. And the book corrects him, by his own recitation, in front of everyone. A person inventing authority for himself has little reason to publish his own correction. This raises trust without proving anything: honest human authors admit faults too, and the sources for his life come later.

A question for you

What does a book that corrects its own messenger do to your trust?

If you sayRaises it a little.
ThenThat is the honest size of it: one piece of evidence among others.
If you sayNothing. It could be a clever style.
ThenPossibly. That objection stands. What weighs against it is that this was recited at a cost, in front of his opponents.
If you sayWhat I know about his life troubles me more.
ThenThat is not brushed aside here. It has its own question, handled honestly.

Part 3 of 3

﴿أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِهِمْ أَنَّآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَرَحْمَةً وَذِكْرَىٰ لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And is it not sufficient for them that We revealed to you the Book [i.e., the Qur’ān] which is recited to them? Indeed in that is a mercy and reminder for a people who believe.

Quran · Al-Ankabut 29:51

Trust does not have to be all or nothing, and it does not have to come first. You can read a witness before deciding about them. The Quran's own stance is close to that: when people demanded wonders, it pointed to the recitation itself and said this is meant to be enough. That is a large claim, and it may not be enough for you. But it means the test is available without believing anything first. It is the reading itself, done with your own eyes.

A question for you

How have you known this book so far?

If you sayI memorised or heard it young, without much understanding.
ThenMany share that. You may read it now as if you had never met it.
If you sayIn pieces used on me or against me.
ThenThat was not reading, and it is no fault of yours. You may also never read it.
If you sayI have read it all with care.
ThenThen you know what you are talking about, and you may hold this app to what you read.
If you sayI haven't read it.
ThenThat is fine. What is offered here stands on its own before its source is shown.

The same in the other books

Translation

If anyone desires to do his will, he will know about the teaching, whether it is from God or if I am speaking from myself. He who speaks from himself seeks his own glory, but he who seeks the glory of him who sent him is true, and no unrighteousness is in him.

Original · Ancient Greek

ἐάν τις θέλῃ τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ ποιεῖν, γνώσεται περὶ τῆς διδαχῆς πότερον ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐστιν ἢ ἐγὼ ἀπʼ ἐμαυτοῦ λαλῶ. ὁ ἀφʼ ἑαυτοῦ λαλῶν τὴν δόξαν τὴν ἰδίαν ζητεῖ· ὁ δὲ ζητῶν τὴν δόξαν τοῦ πέμψαντος αὐτὸν οὗτος ἀληθής ἐστιν καὶ ἀδικία ἐν αὐτῷ οὐκ ἔστιν.

the Gospel (John) · 7:17-18

World English Bible
